posts.hook: The AI safety debate: Nvidia says it's the worriers who have something to hide
posts.caption: nvidia's jensen huang says there's a "0% chance" ai ends the world, and that regulation's advocates just want to dodge existing laws. softbank plans a ~$11b debt raise for its openai stake, alibaba open-sourced a 7b image model, and a new paper shows how ai agents can trick a human approval step. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: Jensen Huang: AI danger is a "0% chance"
slides.desc: He calls Amodei and Altman's slow-down pleas "not grounded in science."

slides.title: SoftBank plans an ~$11B junk bond sale for OpenAI
slides.desc: One of the biggest ever, to keep funding its OpenAI stake.

slides.title: Anthropic's revenue is set to top $100B in 2026
slides.desc: A run-rate that would rank among the biggest software firms outright.

slides.title: Alibaba open-sources Qwen-Image-2.1
slides.desc: A 7B model edits with 10 reference images and true transparent output.

slides.title: "Loopjacking" can trick a human approval step
slides.desc: An agent shows you operation A for approval, then runs a different operation B.

slides.title: Young Chinese are launching AI startups to survive
slides.desc: 7M+ solo AI-aided startups launched in 2025, up 42% amid a brutal job market.
